edits.find:
Asthma and COPD are defined apart by reversibility of airflow obstruction — and reversibility is a measurement, not an impression. That is why spirometry before and after a bronchodilator beats "symptomatic response to a trial of albuterol," even though both involve the same drug: subjective relief does not correlate with the spirometric bronchodilator response.

Notice these stems are deliberately unresolvable clinically — asthma features (seasonal, episodic, eczema, family history) stacked against COPD features (age, pack-years). When the history cannot settle it, the answer must be a test that measures the defining variable, not a proxy marker.
edits.with:
Asthma and COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) are distinguished by reversibility of airflow obstruction. Reversibility is a measurement, not an impression. Therefore, spirometry before and after a bronchodilator is preferred over "symptomatic response to a trial of albuterol," even though both use the same drug. Symptom relief is a poor guide because subjective relief does not correlate with the spirometric bronchodilator response.

When asthma features (seasonal, episodic, eczema, family history) are set against COPD features (age, pack-years), the history cannot settle the diagnosis. The test you order must measure the defining variable, not a proxy marker.
